editorial_sections.h2: Where the Infinity Symbol Comes From
paragraphs: The infinity symbol was introduced by English mathematician John Wallis in 1655, in his work De sectionibus conicis (Treatise on Conic Sections). Wallis used the sideways figure-eight shape, technically called a lemniscate, to represent a quantity without bound.

Why that particular shape isn't fully settled. One theory holds it's a stylized version of the Roman numeral for 1,000 (sometimes written CIƆ or a similar rounded form), which Romans occasionally used loosely to mean "countless." Another points to the lowercase Greek letter omega (ω), the final letter of the Greek alphabet, as a natural symbol for an endpoint that never actually arrives. Whatever its origin, the symbol was adopted quickly and became the universal notation for infinity in calculus and beyond by the 18th century.

editorial_sections.h2: What the Infinity Symbol Means Today
paragraphs: Outside of math, ∞ has settled into a small, consistent set of everyday meanings: endless love, unbreakable friendship, and limitless possibility. It's one of the most common tattoo and jewelry motifs for exactly that reason: a single, simple line with no natural stopping point reads instantly as "forever," which is why it shows up so often on wedding and promise rings, matching couple or best-friend tattoos, and memorial pieces worn in remembrance of someone who died.

A common variation weaves two initials, a name, or a date into the loops of the symbol itself, turning the generic "forever" into something specific to two people or a particular relationship. The symbol also carries a lighter, more general sense of "no limits": used in mottos, brand names, and captions to mean boundless potential rather than a specific bond.

faq.q: What does the infinity symbol mean?
faq.a: ∞ represents something without end or limit: a quantity larger than any number, or a process that never terminates. It's used in mathematics (limits, calculus), and informally to mean "endless" or "forever."

faq.q: How do I type infinity on Windows or Mac?
faq.a: On Windows, hold Alt and type 236 on the numeric keypad (Alt+236). On Mac, press Option+5. In HTML, use the entity ∞ or ∞.

∞ (U+221E) is a plain-text math symbol that renders the same everywhere. ♾️ (U+267E plus a variation selector) is the "infinity emoji": a colorful pictograph that can look completely different across Apple, Google, and Samsung's emoji sets, the same way any other emoji does.
